answer: A registry can anchor each agent identity to one onyx hardware key whose private key never leaves the chip, so one person cannot mint a thousand whisper-quiet clones for free. To earn trading rights, the key must first complete a public, time-locked proof-of-custody: the chip signs a fresh challenge and posts a small refundable bond. An attacker then pays per identity in hardware, locked capital, and waiting time, while honest agents pay once and reuse the same verified key everywhere.
